data.description:
ON CAMERA IN THE WALKTHROUGH. Found by MRQ-81 (surface:268) while walking the full loop from a real public submission — the first time anyone has run that path end to end. Not MRQ-81's files, so filed rather than fixed.

## Symptom

The public conference site renders the speaker name twice, as 'Robin Alvarez · Robin Alvarez'. The API returns the same person id as BOTH Speaker and Submitter for a submission where one person is both — which is the ordinary case for a public CFP submission, so this is the default appearance, not an edge case.

## Why this is critical rather than cosmetic

The walkthrough video IS the evaluation rubric (project CLAUDE.md), and the public conference site is where the 11-step loop ends — it is the payoff shot. A judge sees a duplicated name on the public-facing artifact before they see anything else that was fixed tonight. It is also the single most screenshot-able surface in the product.

It became newly reachable tonight: until PR #30 no public submission could be created at all, so nobody had ever seen a real submitter-is-also-speaker record render on the public site.

## Scope

- One person appearing in two roles on the same submission renders ONCE on the public site.
- Decide deliberately what the public site should say when submitter and speaker genuinely DIFFER — the public site is an audience-facing surface and the submitter is arguably not audience information at all. State the ruling in the PR.
- Check the same duplication does not appear on the agenda, session detail, embeds, or ICS attendee lists — the join is likely shared. A fix that repairs one surface and leaves the embed wrong is worse than none, because the embed is what gets pasted elsewhere.

## Where

src/routes/submissions.queries.ts (the participations join returning the same person id twice) and the public site render path. Cross-check src/ui/public/*.

## Constraints

- Do not dedupe in the view layer alone if the query is returning a duplicate row — fix the source, or the next consumer inherits it.
- Corrected fleet gate: 3x tsc --noEmit, npx vite build, check:design, check:api, trace:ac, plus your diff's own test files. NO full npm test, NO pr-gate; say so in the PR body and let GitHub CI run the suite.
- Test titles must begin 'AC-<n> · ' or 'CONTRACT · '. test.each() fails trace:ac — write tables longhand.
- main is behind a manual merge gate (CODEOWNERS + 'main: manual merge gate'). Open a PR; a human merges.

## Verification

Reproduce on a REAL submission created through /f/cfp (possible as of PR #30), not a seeded one, and confirm the public site, agenda and any embed all render the person once.

data.body: PR #39 — https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/39. Fixed at the source: one shared participant-list builder (src/lib/participants.ts) across public site, embeds, submissions register, board, agenda, and reviewer identity. Ruling: the public site shows speaking roles only; organizer surfaces keep every participant, deduplicated. File answers resolve to filename/type/size with a raster thumbnail behind a preview route that requires the same program access the record does. Validated end to end on a real /f/cfp submission through accept, schedule, publish. Gate: 3x tsc, vite build, check:design, check:api, trace:ac all pass; both suites green locally (worker 258, node 226); no pr-gate per the corrected fleet gate.

Merged as PR #39 (82afc42). Merge-driver review.

FIXED AT THE SOURCE, which is what I asked for and the part that matters: six queries were each hand-rolling the same participations->people join, and they now share src/lib/participants.ts. A view-layer dedupe would have repaired the one screen we happened to look at and left the next consumer inheriting the duplicate. It also fixed an ordering bug nobody had filed — the old ordering tie-broke on a random UUID, so 'the speakers' could reorder between reads.

Coverage confirmed across public site, session and speaker pages, embeds, submissions register, board, agenda and reviewer identity. ICS attendees already used SELECT DISTINCT and never duplicated; now pinned by a test so it cannot regress into the same shape.

THE PUBLIC/ORGANIZER RULING IS RIGHT AND WELL-DRAWN. Public shows SPEAKING ROLES ONLY — a submitter is not audience information. The detail I would have missed: this extends to public NAME SEARCH, so a visitor cannot match a name the page will never print. Organizer surfaces keep every participant, deduplicated, speaking roles first, because dropping a submitter-only participant would blank the Speakers column on a record where they are the only person attached. The record's Participants panel stays unchanged because it is the roster editor and each row already carries its own role label. Three different answers for three different jobs, each argued rather than defaulted.

VALIDATION WAS THE REAL ARTICLE: a genuine /f/cfp submission, logged out, real PNG, then accepted -> scheduled -> published, with BOTH participation rows still in the database and the published session page printing Robin Alvarez once. Proving the duplicate is gone from the render while the underlying rows remain is exactly the right proof — it shows the fix is in the read, not in destroying data.

FIXTURE DEFECT WORTH REMEMBERING: submissions-list and dashboard hand-rolled a schema whose participations table had NO role column, though the real schema has had one since 0001_init. Invisible for as long as nothing read role, then both 500'd the moment something did. A hand-rolled fixture schema silently drifting from the migrations is a latent trap wherever else it exists. Both now seed the duplicate, so the 1,000-row register guards the dedupe at list scale rather than on a toy case.
